intro: In Edirne province stands a building that changed Ottoman architecture: the Üç Şerefeli Mosque and its complex, built in 1437–1447. Here came the first attempt at a central dome on this scale. And look at its four minarets, each one built to a different design.
history: Murad II built this mosque at Edirne between 1437 and 1447, and it marks the turning point of Ottoman architecture. For the first time, a central dome twenty-four metres across was set over the prayer hall, on a six-support system. Now look at the minarets. Each of the four is a different height, with different shaft decoration, and the mosque takes its name from the three balconies on the tallest.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the central dome and the four unlike minarets. Then step into the arcaded courtyard and find the ablution fountain.
facts: Did you know? The tallest minaret contains three separate staircases, one to each balcony, so three muezzins could climb it without ever seeing one another. And this is the building where Ottoman architecture first attempted a central dome twenty-four metres across.
outro: This brings our visit to the Üç Şerefeli Mosque to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this turning point keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
